translation.title: Indometacin Cataplasm (Pap)
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for the analgesic and anti-inflammatory relief of osteoarthritis (degenerative arthritis), periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, epicondylitis of the humerus (such as tennis elbow), muscle pain, and swelling and pain after an injury.
translation.usage: Apply it to the affected area twice a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you have experienced hypersensitivity (asthma, a history of bronchospasm, rhinitis, or angioedema) to aspirin or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, or if the user is a child under 14 years of age. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding, if the user is a child, or if you are hypersensitive to propylene glycol or have experienced such hypersensitivity. Do not use it on skin with lesions (haemorrhagic skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds), on the eyes, or on mucous membranes. Use it externally only. Do not use an occlusive dressing. Itching, redness, rash, contact dermatitis or eczema may occur occasionally, and warmth, swelling, flushing, anaphylaxis, photosensitivity, a burning sensation, irritation, dryness and numbness, gastrointestinal discomfort, headache or dizziness rarely. If any of these occur, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Hypersensitivity reactions (skin reactions, bronchospasm, a drop in blood pressure leading to shock) and, in special cases, aseptic meningitis (headache, nausea, vomiting, fever, a stiff neck, or clouded consciousness) may occur. Symptoms may worsen in patients with psoriasis. Store at room temperature.
